subject: physics
title: Quantum & Nuclear Physics (HL) Adventure 1: Photoelectric effect and de Broglie
welcome_lead: Today you'll kick out photoelectrons and give them a wavelength.
meta_desc: Physics HL — photoelectric effect, work function, Einstein equation, de Broglie λ = h/mv.
final_note: You learned photoelectric: hf = Φ + ½mv²_max; threshold f₀; light has particle (photon) and wave character; de Broglie λ = h/mv.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Shine light on metal → electrons ejected.

Observations puzzle wave theory:
- Only above threshold f₀ ejects e⁻.
- KE_max depends on f, not intensity.
- Intensity controls number ejected.

Einstein (1905): light is photons, each E = hf.

hf = Φ + ½mv²_max
where Φ = work function (depends on metal).

Apply opposing V_s: at V_s, no e⁻ reaches anode.

eV_s = ½mv²_max = hf − Φ.

Plot V_s vs f: straight line, slope = h/e, intercept = -Φ/e. Confirms E = hf — Nobel 1921.

If light has particle nature, do particles have wave nature?

de Broglie (1924): λ = h/p = h/mv.

Electron at 100 V: KE = 100 eV → λ ≈ 0.12 nm (~atomic size) → diffracts through crystals (Davisson-Germer, 1927).

Foundation of electron microscopy.

What is the difference between nuclear fission and fusion?
options: The frequency at which photons travel at the speed of light.
Fission and fusion are the same process, just at different scales.
Fission splits a heavy nucleus into smaller ones; fusion joins light nuclei into a heavier one.
Fission combines small atoms into bigger ones, and fusion splits them.

mcqs.q: If air resistance is ignored, which falls faster: a heavy ball or a light ball dropped from the same height?
options: Heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects because gravity pulls more on them.
The frequency at which photons travel at the speed of light.
Both fall at the same rate because gravitational acceleration is independent of mass.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.

mcqs.q: What is the threshold frequency in the photoelectric effect?
options: The minimum intensity of light needed to eject electrons.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
The minimum frequency of light required to eject electrons from a given metal — it equals the work function divided by Planck's constant.
The frequency at which photons travel at the speed of light.
